5What this report does not prove

  • That this document has been unaltered since it was created in Slack This report's evidence begins at ingest (2026-07-14T02:11:53Z). NemakiWare did not observe any editing, deletion or re-posting that took place inside Slack before that moment. → Reconciliation against Slack's own audit logs (Enterprise Grid audit logs API) — which would in turn rest on trusting a system operated by another organization.
  • That the content is authentic because it arrived over an HMAC-signed webhook An HMAC proves only that the sender held the shared secret. It does not establish that the delivered content matches the record held in Slack, nor that it was unaltered. Authenticating the counterparty and authenticating the content are different claims. → Signed records produced by the source system itself. Slack does not offer this.
  • That the replacement of version 1.0 by version 2.0 was made under proper authority This report records who made the change and when, but whether that person should have held the authority to make it is a judgement for a human to make against the organization's delegation-of-authority rules. → Establishing the rule for who may declare a record authentic (the InterPARES A.6 requirement). Not implemented in this product.
  • That this document is the authoritative copy No rule for identifying the authoritative record is defined in this deployment. Where copies of the same content exist elsewhere, this report does not determine which of them is authoritative. → Defining the identification procedure required by InterPARES A.7 and reflecting that rule in this report.
  • That the document existed at a specific time (a lower time bound) No time-stamp authority is configured in this deployment. The OpenTimestamps proof establishes only an upper bound — that the data existed no later than a given time — and gives no lower bound. → Configuring an RFC 3161 time-stamp authority from an accredited provider.
